Businesses have the right to appeal a rating, to publish a reply alongside it, and to request a re-inspection once improvements have been made, so a rating listed here may since have changed. Each business's current rating is on the Food Standards Agency website.

candidates.source_title: Affordable homes plan refused over harm to Green Belt - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Plans to build 24 affordable homes which would pay homage to a former mill have been refused because of the harm the development would cause to the Green Belt.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to build 24 affordable homes which would pay homage to a former mill have been refused because of the harm the development would cause to the Green Belt. Franstep Limited and David Gibbons applied to Rochdale Council to build 24 apartments and six houses on land at Waterfold Lane, Heap Bridge, just off the M66 motorway. Following discussions with the council, the plans were amended to build 18 three-bed terraced homes and six one-bed apartments instead of 12 two-bed apartments and six three-bed terraced houses. The site was previously occupied by Water Fold Mill from the mid-1800s which was demolished in the late 1960s to early 1970s when the M66 was being built. The area is designated green belt land, on the edge of Heap Bridge village. The proposed development was intended to reflect Victorian mill workers’ cottages and each home was designated to be affordable housing. The application received 16 objections which raised concerns about additional traffic and access to Waterfold Lane, concerns about flood risk and the impact the proposals would have on the area. A planning officer’s report said the development would cause harm to the Green Belt and it would be “car dependent”.

candidates.source_title: Major milestone for Atom Valley as Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre base build completes
candidates.source_summary: Base build completes on the 30,000 sq ft Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre, the first major development within Rochdale’s Atom Valley Innovation District.The centre will connect businesses with specialist facilities, research and investment, with independent analysis forecasting £107 million in economic value over ten years.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major milestone has been reached for Atom Valley with completion of the base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale, which is set to become a nationally significant gateway driving the development of the advanced materials and manufacturing cluster in the region. An error occurred while preparing your download The 30,000 sq ft centre is the first major physical development within the Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID), a 25-acre hub for advanced materials and manufacturing in Rochdale, bringing together businesses, researchers, investors and innovation partners in one location. AVID provides an environment where organisations can innovate, grow and commercialise new technologies, strengthening Greater Manchester's position as a leading centre for advanced materials and manufacturing. Completion of the building represents a major milestone for years of partnership working between Rochdale Development Agency (RDA), Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester and wider innovation partners. RDA has led the physical development of the SMMC, working with partners to secure investment and position advanced materials and manufacturing as a priority opportunity for Rochdale and Greater Manchester. The next phase will see work move from construction towards specialist fit-out ahead of bringing the centre into operation in 2027. The RDA brought together partners from industry, academia and government to establish the Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) in 2023. Since then, businesses have been able to connect with a national network of specialist expertise, facilities and innovation support through the CEAMS partners, including The University of Manchester, the Henry Royce Institute, National Physical Laboratory (NPL), CPI and NCC. CEAMS has already supported more than 90 companies, developing new products and processes and demonstrating the value of a more connected innovation ecosystem. The University is the lead delivery partner charged with delivering the innovation ecosystem that will accelerate the growth of the advanced materials and manufacturing cluster already in the region, connecting our research strengths with businesses and national partners to help new ideas develop, scale and reach the market at pace, and attracting over £60 million in private sector investment. The SMMC and wider Atom Valley Innovation District is a crucial part of our commitment to driving innovation-led growth right across Greater Manchester.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Regulator also vetoes extra Blackpool service, citing lack of space on west coast mainline for new trains to capital Plans to run direct train services to Wrexham and Rochdale from London have been rejected by the rail regulator because of “significant pressure” on the line. The Office of Rail and Road said that there was insufficient space on the crowded west coast mainline to introduce the two new separate train services. It also vetoed plans for additional London-Blackpool train services wanted by Avanti. The ORR had last year knocked back plans for a new independent open access service linking Wrexham and the capital put forward by the Wrexham, Shropshire & Midlands Railway Company (WSMR). WSMR had submitted plans for a slightly less frequent service but the ORR said the new routes would still put the reliability of the wider railway at risk. The new service could have allowed Wrexham to capitalise further on the town’s Hollywood-meets-football mini-boom, fuelled by the Wrexham AFC co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney. Proposals for a new Lumo service between London and Rochdale, again slimmed down after being rejected in 2025, were once more rebuffed. The ORR also said Avanti could not add more Blackpool services from London. However, it did approve one extra London-Chester evening service from Avanti, which would otherwise have run as a “ghost train”, with crew and the rolling stock returning north to the depot overnight. The decision follows the outcry over the ORR’s initial ruling on a Manchester-London service which was barred from taking passengers last year.

Mr O’Regan received both a Pride in the Job Quality Award and a Seal of Excellence from the National House Building Council in 2025, recognising the standards achieved on the development. The visit included an overview of the construction progress and the energy efficient features being built into the homes. The development includes a mix of two, three and four bedroom properties, including apartments and lower cost homes. A total of 268 homes are planned for the site, with 33 designated as affordable housing as part of the planning agreement. Barratt Homes has also committed £156000 towards local community investment to support services and facilities in the surrounding area. James Frith MP said “Visiting Waldmers Wood was a great opportunity to see first hand the high quality homes being delivered here in Bury and to meet the dedicated team behind them. I was especially pleased to congratulate Sean on his well deserved national recognition which reflects the pride and professionalism going into this development. “Schemes like this are vital to helping more people access high quality modern and energy efficient homes. Too many first time buyers feel locked out of the market not because they cannot afford monthly repayments but because they do not have access to large deposits or family support. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Eric Cantona, the M62 and the Industrial Revolution. Despite the long animosity between Lancashire and Yorkshire a few things have successfully made the journey across the Pennines. And to that list you can add the 590 bus . The Rochdale to Halifax service swaps the Roch Valley for the Calder Valley as it crosses over from Greater Manchester into West Yorkshire. And along the way it takes in two marvels of the Industrial Revolution and plenty of the region's most dramatic scenery. I caught the 590 this week as far as Hebden Bridge as part of our occasional series on Greater Manchester's most scenic bus routes . Having stumped up the extra 10 bob, I head upstairs to join a handful of students heading home after lectures on the top deck. From Rochdale bus station it heads east out of the town centre through Smallbridge and Littleborough before crossing the border at Summit into the towns of Walsden, Todmorden and Hebden Bridge. It's a pretty unremarkable start to the journey, but soon the chicken shops and rows of brick terraces start to give way to old weavers cottages and Rochdale's famous flagstone fences. Up ahead the dramatic gritstone ridge of Blackstone Edge, marking the border between Greater Manchester and West Yorkshire, looms on the horizon. At Littleborough the bus turns north and as we begin the head into the hills we pass the former studio of the late Walter Kershaw. In 1984 it was also the scene of one of the biggest underground fires in transport history when a train carrying a million litres of petrol derailed. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Residents have raised concerns about a fast-food restaurant’s late-licence plan. Rochdale Council has received an application for the Burger Box, at the former Haibat Sultan restaurant at 26 Milkstone Road, to stay open until 3am daily. The council’s Licensing Sub-Committee will meet on Monday, October 12, to determine the application which names Kashif Hazarbuz as the premises licence holder. The Burger Box is described as a fast-food restaurant in a ground-floor retail unit with residential accommodation above, situated on a busy main road. Planning permission has been granted for eat-in, collection and delivery service from 11am to 11pm Monday to Sunday, and 11am to 10pm on Sundays and bank holidays. The licensing application looks to extend this to 3am each day. Under the terms of the premises licence, no alcohol can be taken into or be consumed in the restaurant at any time. Among the objections, Mrs S Rana believes that that there will be an increase in anti-social behaviour and noise from the restaurant. She is also concerned that there will be an increase in traffic and pollution if the licence is granted until 3am. Mr I Hussain believes the premises may attract anti-social behaviour within the area and lead to an increase of crime and disorder. He has concerns that the premises will create a public nuisance to residents especially with the late-night hours. He believes the licence should end at 11pm.

Chancerygate has appointed Barnfield Construction as the main contractor for the new Birch 100 unit, with practical completion expected in summer 2027. The unit is targeting BREEAM Excellent and an EPC A rating and will feature solar photovoltaic panels and electric vehicle charging. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rugby veterans will be tackling an epic trek to help charities close to their hearts this month. Rochdale Rugby League Masters — which includes over-35s men’s and women’s teams — will be stepping out for the 45-mile All Together Walk 2026 in aid of the MND Association, Rugby League Cares Brain Health Fund, Springhill Hospice and Rochdale Masters. Last year, the group walked from Rochdale to Blackpool, raising just over £9,000. This year, the goal is to beat £10,000. More than 25 walkers are expected to set off from Ince Rosebridge Rugby League Club in Wigan, before covering 45 miles and visiting eight masters clubs along the route, including Leigh East, Cadishead Rhinos, Salford City Roosters, Bury Broncos and ending at Rochdale Masters Club at Mayfield Sports Centre in Keswick Street, Rochdale. Walk organiser Carl Abraham said: “Everyone is invited to join us. “You can take on the full 45 miles or simply join the group for one stage or two. Whether you are a player, supporter, friend or simply want to support the cause, everyone is welcome.” As well as encouraging people to take part on the day, the club is looking for local businesses to sponsor the event.
